entries.definition: A closed trainable ReasonCode explaining why an adjudication refused a call; POLICY_BLOCK means an explicit policy rule denied it.

contrasts.explanation: A refusal reason is a closed ABI label; a DOS decision kind classifies an operator queue row and its resolver lifecycle.
ReasonCode labels adjudication semantics; a hook gate class declares which tree surface a hook may mutate.
A refusal reason explains a tool-call decision; a policy posture verdict is the ALLOW/DENY result of folding organization amendment authority.

entries.definition: A persistent DOS row category identifying arbitration refusal work whose resolution depends on the current lane-lease state.

contrasts.explanation: ARBITER_REFUSE classifies a DOS decision row; it is not a ReasonCode in the kernel adjudication ABI.
A DOS decision kind persists arbitration state; a hook gate class controls execution isolation for a checker.
A DOS decision kind drives resolver lifecycle and history, not an ALLOW/DENY policy amendment result.

entries.definition: A provider account-capacity slot with availability, session cap, leased slots, free slots, and bound worker IDs.

contrasts.explanation: A seat supplies bounded account capacity; it is not the worker process consuming one slot.

entries.definition: The normalized behavior state off, shadow, or on; it is always interpreted within the owning domain and does not imply lifecycle authority or maturity.

contrasts.explanation: Activation posture is a three-state operating switch; maturity is a domain-specific readiness ladder and may advance independently.
Activation posture states whether behavior runs; lifecycle class states the authority role of the indexed definition.

entries.definition: The typed per-call result emitted by the adjudication fold: allow, deny, transform, quarantine, require-witness, defer, or indeterminate, with a reason and deciding rung.

contrasts.explanation: The verdict states what happens; the reason code explains why that outcome was selected.
A verdict records the result for one call; the capability floor bounds authority before that decision is made.
A verdict is produced for one call; a declaration is reusable configuration consulted while producing it.

entries.definition: The fak management boundary that governs model traffic, tool effects, context, and recovery.

contrasts.explanation: An arithmetic routine executed by a processor; it does not govern an agent's tool effects.

entries.definition: A durable, addressable agent execution record carrying drive state and pointers without storing the provider transcript.

contrasts.explanation: The session is the durable execution identity; resume is one transition that re-admits a paused session.

entries.definition: The minimum authority boundary represented by negotiated capability tokens and policy constraints; it limits what may proceed but does not describe the outcome of a particular call.

contrasts.explanation: A capability is authority advertised or granted ahead of a call; a verdict is the call-specific result after checks run.
The floor is the effective authority boundary; a declaration is one configured input used to establish it.

entries.definition: A capability-readiness level in the ordered proposed, prototyped, tested, dogfooded, default ladder; measurement remains an orthogonal badge rather than another rung.

contrasts.explanation: Maturity is an ordered readiness ladder; activation posture is the independent off, shadow, or on operating state.
A maturity rung grades operational readiness of a capability; index lifecycle class grades the authority role of terminology evidence.

entries.definition: A transport-agnostic roster of uniquely identified controllable machines whose live reports are folded by the public fleet core.

contrasts.explanation: A fleet is the available machine roster; a wave is one concurrency-safe batch of work selected for launch.

entries.definition: An arithmetic routine executed by a processor.

contrasts.explanation: The fak management boundary governs agent behavior; it is not a processor arithmetic routine.

entries.definition: A context-window event that replaces prior history so resident input falls while cumulative usage and transcript bytes may continue rising.

contrasts.explanation: Compaction reduces resident model context; a recovery checkpoint preserves typed continuation state for rerouting or repair.

entries.definition: The internal/disambiguation package, named as a contrast target for the CLI-scoped kernel entry.

contrasts.explanation: The package and CLI-scoped kernel are distinct.

entries.definition: A named taxonomy partition that maps a work request to a canonical file-tree region and concurrency policy.

contrasts.explanation: The lane names the work partition; a lease is the time-bounded ownership claim that currently holds it or its tree.

entries.definition: A durable recurring dispatch state machine identified by loop ID and measured through admitted, refused, started, ended, and witnessed runs.

contrasts.explanation: A loop owns recurring execution state for one cadence; a supervisor observes multiple witnessed surfaces and decides interventions.

entries.definition: A declared file-tree region used to arbitrate concurrent work; it may own several leaves and must not be inferred from a similar name.

contrasts.explanation: A lane controls collision-safe admission; a leaf provides semantic attribution and may map into that lane.

entries.definition: An indexed, bounded batch of dispatch members with a shared step budget and explicit lease regions or whole-lane claims.

contrasts.explanation: A wave is a selected launch batch; the fleet is the machine population on which batches may execute.

entries.definition: One executing worker record with structured issue, lane, backend, and witnessed-result fields; its free-form output is untrusted narration.

contrasts.explanation: A worker is one execution process; a seat is provider-account capacity that may host multiple worker sessions.

entries.definition: A reviewed exported type, function, variable, or constant from non-test, non-generated Go source that may warrant canonical or incidental terminology classification.

contrasts.explanation: An exported symbol is discovered from a public Go declaration; a capability token is an explicit runtime negotiation declaration and need not be an exported identifier.

entries.definition: The fak command-line product surface, named as a contrast target for the package-scoped kernel entry.

contrasts.explanation: The CLI surface and package-scoped kernel are distinct.

entries.definition: The validated (fak <leaf>) commit-subject token binding one commit to its semantic leaf; it is not a lane lease or module version.

contrasts.explanation: A stamp attributes a commit to a leaf; module@rev identifies the history-derived version after commits land.

entries.definition: The fak-enabled treatment measured against a declared alternative; calling it a baseline obscures which arm is the comparator.

contrasts.explanation: The fak arm is the treatment; the naive baseline is only contextual floor evidence.
The fak arm is the treatment; the tuned baseline is the credible comparator.

entries.definition: A decision layer whose input is witnessed liveness, worker verdicts, escalations, and leases; missing witnesses cause escalation rather than inference.

contrasts.explanation: The supervisor reasons over witnessed fleet state; a loop is one recurring execution state machine it may observe or act on.

entries.definition: A hook-runner classification declaring whether a gate mutates the index/worktree, intentionally uses a worktree, or is a tree-twin checker.

contrasts.explanation: LANDS_TREE declares hook execution scope; it is not a reason why a model tool call was refused.
A hook class is local runner metadata; a DOS decision kind is a persisted arbitration or resolver category.
A hook class schedules and isolates gate execution; it does not grant or deny organization policy authority.

entries.definition: The authority status of a disambiguation entry: current, versioned, research, or archived; it says what role the source may play, not whether a feature is enabled.

contrasts.explanation: Lifecycle class states an entry's authority and historical role; activation posture states whether behavior is off, shadowing, or on.
Index lifecycle class governs terminology evidence; a capability maturity rung describes how operationally mature a product capability is in its own domain.

entries.definition: The fak command-line product surface for operating the agent kernel.

contrasts.explanation: The command-line product surface is not the internal Go package API.

entries.definition: The internal/disambiguation Go package that validates and queries public terminology records.

contrasts.explanation: The package API is not the fak command-line product surface.

entries.definition: A live ownership claim carrying lease ID, lane or tree, holder identity, and read-only posture for collision admission.

contrasts.explanation: A lease is an active holder claim; the lane is the durable taxonomy partition it may claim.

entries.definition: The semantic package or command unit that owns a change and supplies the attribution token in a valid fak commit stamp.

contrasts.explanation: A leaf identifies what semantic unit changed; a lane is the concurrency ownership region that admits work.

entries.definition: Kernel-owned per-layer attention key/value tensors indexed by token position and invalidated or rewritten when the model sequence changes.

contrasts.explanation: The model KV cache is directly owned and mutable inside fak; provider prompt caching is an upstream reuse service exposed as billed token axes.
A KV cache is one sequence's live attention state; the radix cache indexes token prefixes and references reusable snapshots across requests.
The KV cache contains model attention state, not completed tool outputs or world-versioned effects.

entries.definition: A semantic assessment whose result depends on a model interpreting content or intent; it is distinct from fak's deterministic structural preflight and is not part of the preflight command's local fold.

contrasts.explanation: A model-mediated check depends on model inference; structural preflight reaches its verdict from local grammar and adjudicator rules with no model in the loop.

entries.definition: A history-derived identity rendered as module@r<touch-count>+g<commit>, naming which module moved and at what revision.

contrasts.explanation: A module is the versioned path surface; a leaf is the semantic owner used for attribution and stamps.

entries.definition: A comparison arm representing the untuned or resend-everything floor; useful context, but never the decision-grade headline alternative.

contrasts.explanation: A baseline is an alternative being compared; the fak arm is the measured treatment whose gain is claimed.
The naive arm is a floor; the tuned arm is the credible next-best option an operator would actually choose.

entries.definition: A scoped value statement graded against the real tuned alternative and stated net of introduced costs, with provenance, reproduction witness, and realization status.

contrasts.explanation: The tuned baseline answers only what the claim is compared against; net-true grading requires all six claim dimensions.
Provenance answers only how the value was obtained; a net-true claim also names baseline, net cost, scope, witness, and realization.

entries.definition: A string explicitly registered by a public package as a negotiated ABI capability; it is inventory evidence, not automatically a canonical term or an authorization verdict.

contrasts.explanation: A capability token comes from explicit RegisterCapability declarations; an exported symbol candidate comes from the package's reviewed public identifier surface.

entries.definition: A declarative set of tool, argument, network, and resource rules loaded by the adjudicator; it states configured constraints but is not itself a decision for one call.

contrasts.explanation: A declaration is input to adjudication; a verdict is the typed result for one tool call.
A policy declaration supplies configured rules; the capability floor is the minimum authority those rules allow a caller to exercise.

entries.definition: The ALLOW or DENY result of folding compiled, environment, and organization authority over a policy amendment.

contrasts.explanation: The posture verdict is the decision result; POLICY_BLOCK is one explanatory reason attached to a separate tool-call refusal vocabulary.
A posture verdict resolves one policy fold; a DOS decision kind categorizes persistent arbitration or operator work.
ALLOW/DENY describes policy authority, not whether a hook lands the tree or operates in a worktree twin.

entries.definition: An upstream provider-owned prompt-prefix reuse service observed as cache-read and cache-creation token accounting with provider TTL and pricing rules.

contrasts.explanation: Provider prompt cache state is not directly addressable tensor memory in fak and cannot be edited like the kernel-owned KV cache.
Provider cache lifetime and identity are upstream contracts; the radix prefix cache is fak-owned, namespace-keyed, and explicitly budgeted and evicted.
Provider prompt caching reuses model input prefixes outside fak; the tool-result cache locally serves completed tool outputs under effect-aware invalidation.

entries.definition: A fak-owned radix tree that longest-prefix-matches namespaced token sequences to reusable KV snapshots under token and byte budgets.

contrasts.explanation: The radix cache is a multi-prefix lookup and residency index; a model KV cache is the live tensor state for one sequence.
The radix cache is namespace-scoped, budgeted, and evicted by fak; provider prompt caching is controlled upstream and reported through cache read/write usage.
The radix cache keys token-prefix paths and snapshot residency; the tool-result cache keys tool calls plus effect epochs.

entries.definition: A typed snapshot of goal, pending turn, continuation, generation, and state revision emitted when session recovery is requested.

contrasts.explanation: The checkpoint preserves control-plane continuation state; compaction rewrites model-visible history to reduce resident context.
The checkpoint is evidence and continuation data for recovery, not the repair or reroute action itself.

entries.definition: The host-side agent application loop that turns model completions into tool calls and final answers through the Planner seam.

contrasts.explanation: The agent application runtime drives the task loop; the agent kernel mediates its model and tool effects at the enforcement boundary.

entries.definition: The configured gateway server that exposes HTTP or MCP transport, authentication, routing, kernel mediation, and observability.

contrasts.explanation: The gateway runtime is a long-lived transport server; the fak CLI kernel is the command surface used to configure and launch it.

entries.definition: The wrapper process that launches a guest command under fak policy, hook, capability, and stop-gate enforcement.

contrasts.explanation: The guard runtime enforces a launched process; an agent session is the durable execution identity and state pointers that may outlive one wrapper process.

entries.definition: The model-completion implementation behind an engine driver, such as an on-device llama.cpp or Ollama adapter that generates text for one turn.

contrasts.explanation: The model-serving runtime executes completion; the model KV cache is attention state owned or reused during that execution.

entries.definition: The dispatch worker process that selects a backend, optionally wraps it with fak guard, and executes one lane-scoped work packet.

contrasts.explanation: The worker runtime executes admitted work; a DOS decision kind classifies persisted arbitration or resolver state about whether work may proceed.

entries.definition: A bounded repair or reroute response when persisted or cumulative session state cannot safely continue unchanged.

contrasts.explanation: Recovery is the repair action; a recovery checkpoint is the structured continuation state handed to that action.
Recovery responds to corrupt or over-envelope state; resume merely re-admits a valid paused session.

entries.definition: The paused-to-running boundary that re-admits an existing session using warm KV when available or a safe cold re-prefill.

contrasts.explanation: Resume changes the run state of an existing session; it is not the session identity or transcript.
Resume continues a valid paused session; recovery repairs or reroutes state that cannot safely continue as-is.

entries.definition: Stand-in data explicitly labeled SIMULATED; it can test a path but cannot be narrated as a witnessed real-world measurement.

contrasts.explanation: Simulation status says how evidence was produced; net-true status grades the entire scoped claim.
SIMULATED is one provenance value; witness provenance is the full closed classification field.

entries.definition: The local pre-dispatch fold over grammar and adjudicator rungs for one tool call, producing a verdict without executing the tool or asking a model to interpret intent.

contrasts.explanation: Preflight is the checking operation; the adjudication verdict is its typed output.
Structural preflight applies deterministic local rules before dispatch; a model-mediated check asks a model to classify meaning or intent.

entries.definition: A fak-owned cache of completed tool-call results keyed by tool, argument hash, principal when isolated, and world-version epochs.

contrasts.explanation: The tool-result cache stores tool outputs and invalidates on modeled world changes; the KV cache stores per-token attention tensors.
The tool-result cache is kernel-owned and directly invalidated by fak epochs; provider prompt-cache entries are externally owned and observed through usage accounting.
The tool-result cache looks up effect-safe tool calls; the radix cache longest-prefix-matches token sequences to reusable model snapshots.

entries.definition: The best-practice alternative an operator would actually run, required as the decision-grade comparator for a performance headline.

contrasts.explanation: The tuned baseline is the next-best alternative; the fak arm is the treatment being evaluated against it.
The tuned baseline reflects credible optimization; the naive baseline is only an untuned floor.

entries.definition: The closed label stating how a reported value was obtained: witnessed, observed, modeled, or simulated; it does not replace a reproduction witness.

contrasts.explanation: Provenance answers how a number was obtained; net-true grading also requires baseline, net cost, scope, witness, and realization.
Provenance is the classification carried by evidence; simulated evidence is one explicitly labeled provenance class.
